extracted.intended_audience: learned readers, natural philosophers, and physicians
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative principles for conducting and improving the sciences of medicine and human philosophy: what to study, how to record and judge practice, and methodological cautions about superstition and invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medicine must be grounded in natural philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: The science of medicine, if destituted and forsaken by natural philosophy, is not much better than an empirical practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medicine should be integrated with natural philosophy (theoretical understanding), not left as mere empirical or superstitious practice; grounding in theory distinguishes science from mere empiricism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human philosophy should study mind–body sympathies
rubrics_metrics.description: Human nature as a distinct knowledge is chiefly fit to inquire concerning the sympathies and concordances between the mind and body, which being mixed cannot be properly assigned to the sciences of either.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate a distinct branch of human philosophy to study how mind and body disclose and impress upon one another (discovery and impression). This includes physiological psychology and psychosomatics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physiognomy should include gestures/motions, not just lineaments
rubrics_metrics.description: Aristotle handled the 'factures' (lineaments) of the body but not the gestures of the body, which disclose present humour and state of the mind and will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study facial and bodily motions systematically: gestures and countenance reveal present states more precisely than static lineaments and are useful for detecting dissimulation and guiding business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate impressions between humours and mind (reciprocal effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider how the humours and affects of the body alter or work upon the mind, and how the passions or apprehensions of the mind alter or work upon the body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research both directions of influence—bodily states on mental states and mental states on bodily states—particularly imagination's capacity to alter the body, while remaining cautious about claims of miraculous cures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record and continue medicinal history (case narratives)
rubrics_metrics.description: The discontinuance of the ancient diligence of Hippocrates, who set down narratives of special cases and how they proceeded, is a deficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physicians should keep case histories and continuations of medical observations (neither infinite nor reserved only for wonders) so that new but not unique phenomena are recorded for future guidance, similar to the legal practice of reporting cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anatomy must study diversities, secrecies, humours' nests, and disease footprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Anatomists inquire of parts and collocations but not of the diversities of the parts, secrecies of the passages, seats or nestling of the humours, nor of the footsteps and impressions of diseases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative, multiple anatomies are required to observe internal variations, subtle passages (often latent in dead bodies), cavities where humours lodge, and the internal traces of disease (abscesses, ulcers, putrefactions, consumptions, contractions, stones, worms). Consider dissections (including of beasts, and where possible with living observations) and gather many observations to capture these differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not abandon inquiry into cures judged 'incurable'
rubrics_metrics.description: In the inquiry of diseases they abandon the cures of many, pronouncing some incurable and thereby enacting a law of neglect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate potential cures, even for extreme cases or those commonly deemed incurable; avoid institutionalized neglect that protects ignorance from discredit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physician's duty includes mitigation of pain and attendance at death
rubrics_metrics.description: The office of a physician is not only to restore health but to mitigate pain and dolors, and to give attendances to facilitate and assuage pains and agonies of death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physicians should research and provide palliative care and humane attendance in dying, not abandon patients once recovery is deemed unlikely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve and standardize effective receipts/experimental medicines
rubrics_metrics.description: Physicians have frustrated the fruit of tradition and experience by changing quid pro quâ in their receipts; they have not set down certain experimental medicines for particular diseases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document, preserve, and transmit tried remedies tied to particular diseases rather than continually altering recipes; combine learning and empirical tradition by delivering certain experimentally validated medicines alongside theoretical prescriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitate and systematize mineral baths and medicinable fountains by art
rubrics_metrics.description: Although mineral medicines are extolled and natural baths are medicinable, no man hath sought to make an imitation by art of natural baths and medicinable fountains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate which minerals impart virtues to medicinal waters (sulphur, vitriol, steel, etc.) and develop controlled compositions to reproduce and command these virtues artificially for greater variety and safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Therapeutic regimens must be ordered, pursued, and sustained
rubrics_metrics.description: Prescripts in use are too compendious; it is a vain opinion to think any medicine so sovereign that a single receipt will work great effect; it is order, pursuit, sequence, and interchange of application that is mighty in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design cures as sustained regimens with sequence and exchange of applications; ensure precise prescribing and patient obedience rather than ad-hoc daily devices; truth of direction must precede severity of observance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cosmetic/art of decoration should aim at cleanliness, use, and wholesomeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Cosmetic (art of decoration) hath parts civil and parts effeminate; artificial decoration is often neither fine enough to deceive, nor handsome to use, nor wholesome to please.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cosmetic arts should prioritize cleanliness (social and personal reverence), practical usefulness, and healthiness rather than mere deceptive or effeminate ornament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophical inquiry into athletic (bodily) practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Practices of athletic ability are known, but the philosophy concerning them is not much inquired; they are supposed gained by nature or by continual custom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study the methods and principles behind bodily strengths, swiftness, endurance, and pain tolerance to determine teachable techniques versus innate aptness; investigate rather than assume outcomes are only natural or habitual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arts of pleasure require social/legal restraint
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief deficiency in arts of pleasure sensual is of laws to repress them; games of recreation belong to civil life and education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the need for legal and societal frameworks to moderate voluptuary arts and sensual practices; preserve recreations as part of civil education but check excesses that indicate moral decline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inquiry into the soul must be guided by religion to avoid deceit
rubrics_metrics.description: Although knowledge of the nature and state of the soul may be inquired into by nature, in the end it must be hounded by religion, or else it will be subject to deceit and delusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When investigating metaphysical questions like the origin and immortality of the soul, temper natural inquiry with theological consideration to prevent misleading conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish artificial (rational) from superstitious divination
rubrics_metrics.description: Divination is artificial when the mind maketh a prediction by argument (rational) or by experimental coincidence (often superstitious); natural divination is presentation by internal power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor predictions grounded in derivations of causes (rational inference) over mere coincidental correlations (experimental coincidences); treat 'coincidence-based' divination with skepticism as often superstitious (e.g., inspections of sacrifices, bird flights, Chaldean astrology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat claims about imagination/fascination with methodological and moral caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Fascination is the power of imagination intensive upon other bodies; some schools exalt imagination into miracle-working. Ceremonies may fortify imagination but may be unlawful if they propose noble effects by easy observances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate the transmission and effect of imagination (possible natural operations from spirit to spirit) but avoid endorsing magic or ceremonies as shortcuts that oppose moral injunctions (e.g., labour vs. easy observances). Distinguish genuine natural mechanisms from superstition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a science of imagination and arts intellectual (invention, judgment, memory, elocution)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no proper science that fits the imagination; the arts intellectual are four—art of invention, examination/judgment, custody/memory, and elocution/tradition; the art of invention is found wanting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish systematic methods for the imagination and for the art of invention so that discovery is an art (teachable and reproducible) rather than mere chance; logic should aim to invent sciences and axioms (not merely judge existing ones).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention should be an art, not left to chance
rubrics_metrics.description: Invention (of arts and sciences) is deficient; historically particulars were infinite and inventions referred more to chance than to art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create methods and disciplines dedicated to invention/discovery (analogous to the mariner's needle enabling exploration): teach and systematize procedures that lead to new sciences and useful inventions rather than relying on accidental discovery.
